stories.headline: Trump administration asks US Supreme Court to allow White House ballroom work
stories.title: Trump administration asks US Supreme Court to allow White House ballroom work
stories.summary: The Trump administration has asked the US Supreme Court to allow construction of a USD 400 million White House ballroom to continue while it appeals a lower court order halting aboveground work, arguing the project is essential for national security
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

event term: 'national security' in summary weight 42
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: Washington: President Donald Trump’s administration on Friday asked the US Supreme Court to allow the White House to continue construction on its USD 400 million ballroom project while it appeals a lower court’s order to halt the work.
Trump’s solicitor general petitioned the high court to suspend last week’s decision by a three-judge panel from the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit.
Chief Justice John Roberts set a deadline of Tuesday for a response by plaintiffs challenging the ballroom project.
The divided appeals court panel ruled last week Trump must stop the White House ballroom’s construction because Congress has not approved the project.

The panel’s majority said Trump doesn’t have the unilateral authority to build a 90,000-square-foot (8,400-square-metre) ballroom where the White House’s East Wing stood before he ordered its demolition last fall.
The lower court suspended its own ruling for two weeks to give Trump’s Republican administration time to appeal to the Supreme Court.
Solicitor General D John Sauer asked the Supreme Court to rule on its stay petition before the appeals court panel’s decision takes effect on August 21.

“This case involves an extraordinary and unlawful injunction that will halt the ongoing construction of the integrated military complex, including a totally secure ballroom space, at the East Wing of the White House, which is vitally required by national security,” Sauer wrote.
In April, a district court judge ordered a stop to aboveground construction of the planned ballroom.
But the judge stressed that the White House was free to proceed with underground work, including the construction of any bunkers, military installations and medical facilities.
The DC Circuit panel’s 2-1 decision upheld an order to pause aboveground construction on the project, siding with historic preservationists who sued to stop construction of the ballroom.

“Whether or not a massive ballroom should be constructed is for Congress to decide and is not a matter for Executive self-help,” wrote the majority’s two judges, both appointed by Democratic presidents.

stories.headline: Supreme Court urges Kuki, Meitei groups to make peace, remove blockade on highways
stories.title: Supreme Court urges Kuki, Meitei groups to make peace, remove blockade on highways
stories.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant says highways act as a lifeline for ordinary people; the court says it does not want to pass any sweeping directions which may unsettle the State again
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'chief justice' in summary weight 25.2
event term: 'chief justice of india' in summary weight 27.6
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (August 14, 2026) urged both Kuki and Meitei groups to work for peace, remove the blockades on National Highways heading to Manipur, and allow essentials to reach the northeastern State affected by ethnic violence since May 2023.
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, heading a three-judge Bench, said highways act as a lifeline for ordinary people.

The court was hearing a petition filed by the Kuki Women Organisation for Human Rights seeking the removal of the blockade on National Highway 2 and restoration of supply of essential services to the State.
“Why can’t both groups realise something?
That blockade of the highway does not serve either group.
With the intervention of some agency, why can’t you allow the NH to open,” the CJI asked both groups represented by their respective counsel.
Impleading the National Highway Authority of India in the case, the Bench asked the parties to “think of peace now”.
It has also sought a clarification from the parties on whether there were any other blocked highways to Manipur.
Senior advocate Anand Grover, for the petitioner NGO, said the situation was almost desperate with the lack of essential supplies hitting the lives of the people in Manipur.
The court, while agreeing with Mr. Grover about the dire situation, said it did not want to pass any sweeping directions which may unsettle the State again.

stories.headline: Kishan Reddy alleges attempts to incite attacks on Parliament, Supreme Court
stories.title: Kishan Reddy alleges attempts to incite attacks on Parliament, Supreme Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Union Minister for Coal and Mines G. Kishan Reddy on Friday alleged that ‘certain malicious elements’ were conspiring to ‘incite attacks’ on Parliament and the Supreme Court, hoping to create a situation in India similar to the political turmoil witnessed in countries such as Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Nepal.

He further claimed that ‘some Opposition forces’ within the country were ‘distressed’ by India’s progress, much like Pakistan and Bangladesh, which, he said, viewed India’s development with envy and anxiety at the National Tricolour Rally (Tiranga Yatra) organised by the Telangana BJP from the Dr. B.R. Ambedkar statue at Tank Bund to the Swami Vivekananda statue on the eve of Independence Day.

The Union Minister alleged that people were aware of how certain political parties and what he termed ‘Tukde-Tukde gangs’ had behaved during the events surrounding Operation Sindoor, claiming that they appeared to ‘want Pakistan to succeed and India to fail’.
“The people of the nation must reject the malicious politics of those who carry the Constitution in hand while engaging in anti-national conspiracies,” he said.
Calling for unity, Mr. Kishan Reddy said the need of the hour was for citizens to work together for the nation’s progress under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
He also challenged Chief Minister.
A. Revanth Reddy to take action against the AIMIM for allegedly opposing the singing of Vande Mataram.

Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar said the Congress should demonstrate its commitment to youth empowerment by providing opportunities to members of Generation Z in the State Cabinet.
Stating that there was broad agreement on the proposal to permit entry into legislative bodies at the age of 21, he called for a nationwide discussion on the issue.
Mr. Sanjay Kumar also urged the Congress to field Gen Z candidates in the forthcoming MLC elections and give greater representation to younger leaders while allotting Assembly tickets.
Telangana BJP president N. Ramchander Rao extended Independence Day greetings to the people of the State and thanked participants for joining the Tiranga Yatra with enthusiasm and discipline.
Rajya Sabha member and BJP OBC Morcha national president K. Laxman said India’s strength lay in its unity despite its linguistic, religious, regional and cultural diversity.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Imposes Rs. 10 Lakh Cost On Reliance Industries Ltd For Obstructing 20-Year-Old NTPC Suit
stories.title: Supreme Court Imposes Rs. 10 Lakh Cost On Reliance Industries Ltd For Obstructing 20-Year-Old NTPC Suit
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (August 14) imposed a cost of Rs.
for prolonging a 20-year-old commercial suit filed by NTPC.
The cost imposed was directed to be deposited with the Supreme Court Advocates on Record Association.

A bench of Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe strongly disapproved of RIL's litigation strategy, noting that the suit filed in 2005 is still at the evidence stage, with the company raising objections at every turn.
“The following facts would reveal that the power of the RIL to litigate and obstruct progress of the suit seems unlimited.

There is no dearth of financial resources, no obligation to aid and assist the court to cope with pending backlog of cases, perhaps it is lucrative for RIL to raise some objection or the other at every stage and when the trial court rejects it, the appellate and special leave jurisdictions open up…it is compelling for us to note that the suit filed by NTPC way back in 2005 has not progressed much.
At every stage there has been obstruction… In all, two decades have passed by and the suit is still at the stage of evidence.”, the Court observed.
The dispute arises out of a 2005 suit filed by NTPC against Reliance Industries Ltd.
(RIL) seeking specific performance of a natural gas supply agreement.
Despite being pending for more than 20 years, the suit has not proceeded beyond the evidence stage.
During the course of the proceedings, RIL filed a series of applications and appeals challenging various procedural orders.

First, it sought discovery of NTPC's internal documents, but the application was rejected by both the Single Judge and the Division Bench as a belated "fishing enquiry." RIL subsequently attempted to introduce its own internal documents on record, but that request was also rejected, and its challenge before the Supreme Court was later withdrawn.
